title: BET bromodomain inhibition as a therapeutic strategy to target c-Myc
central_claims: BET bromodomain inhibition with JQ1 suppresses MYC transcription and proliferation in multiple myeloma and improves efficacy in mouse models, motivating a therapeutic strategy.

source_manifest.title: Replication Study: BET bromodomain inhibition as a therapeutic strategy to target c-Myc
source_manifest.finding: JQ1-mediated MYC downregulation and improved mouse survival reproduced; tumor-burden significance did not, with early control deaths limiting that endpoint.

source_manifest.title: Potent antimyeloma activity of the novel bromodomain inhibitors I-BET151 and I-BET762.
source_manifest.finding: Independent I-BET151/I-BET762 experiments show MYC repression, antiproliferative effects and mouse survival benefit; primary abstract read.

source_manifest.title: Bromodomain inhibitor OTX015 in patients with lymphoma or multiple myeloma: a dose-escalation, open-label, pharmacokinetic, phase1 study.
source_manifest.finding: The dose-escalation trial enrolled45 patients including12 with myeloma; thrombocytopenia and other toxicities limited dosing. A clinical trial does not establish the original strategy as routine successful therapy.
